items.summary: Millimeter-wave communications technology and solutions provider TMY Technology (Tmytek) officially listed on Taiwan's Innovation Board on September 22 at an offering price of NT$60 (approx. US$1.90) per share. The company said its products, which span millimeter-wave R&D and validation instruments, Lego-like phased-array antennas and subsystem modules, have moved from development and verification into commercial delivery and mass production.

items.title: Changs Ascending eyes AI data center backup power, storage growth
items.summary: Changs Ascending's board approved an operating plan on Sept. 21 to launch an energy systems integration push into the AI data center sector, betting on structurally rising demand from AI computing centers for stable power, backup power, and ESS. The lithium battery materials maker aims to extend its proven UPS, lithium iron phosphate battery and BESS integration capabilities in semiconductor sites into AI data center power infrastructure as the next growth engine for its energy business.

items.title: Meta's AI agent Muse tops app charts, driving AMD's market cap past US$1 trillion
items.summary: Meta's new AI agent, Muse, has leapt to the top of app charts roughly two weeks after its release. Its popularity has helped push up chip stocks by focusing attention on the importance of CPUs for agentic AI.

items.title: Hermes Testing sees growth opportunity in AI-driven chip demand as OTC debut expands reach
items.summary: Hermes Testing Solutions began trading on the over-the-counter market on September 22, positioning itself to benefit from rising demand tied to artificial intelligence and high-performance computing. The semiconductor wafer testing provider is also expanding into high-speed memory SLT, advanced packaging equipment, and SiPh CPO testing.

items.title: Unitree targets humanoid robots' next bottleneck with 22-DoF Dex5-S hand
items.summary: Humanoid robot makers are accelerating investment in dexterous hands as the component becomes increasingly important to fine manipulation. Chinese robotics company Unitree Robotics launched its new Dex5-S dexterous hand on September 21, raising the degrees of freedom to 22 and adopting dimensions close to those of a human hand. items.title: Acer debuts first Googlebook with 360-degree hinge
items.summary: Acer has launched its first Googlebook, a new flagship notebook equipped with Gemini Intelligence that combines premium materials, strong performance, smart features, and seamless syncing with Android phones. The Acer Googlebook 14 is also the first convertible Googlebook on the market.

items.title: Microsoft opens fourth India cloud region, casting Hyderabad as an AI hub for Asia and the Global South
items.summary: Microsoft has turned a headline slice of its US$20.5 billion India commitment into operating infrastructure, opening a Hyderabad cloud region it intends to serve customers well beyond India's borders. The move positions the country as a supply base for AI compute at a moment when it generates far more data than it can process at home.

items.title: Hanmi Semiconductor ships first FC Bonder 75 for 2.5D packaging
items.summary: Hanmi Semiconductor said on September 22 that it has shipped its first FC Bonder 75 to a customer, expanding the South Korean equipment maker's reach beyond high-bandwidth memory (HBM) into the broader system semiconductor packaging market.

items.title: Alibaba speeds V900 rollout, targeting 20GW of data centers
items.summary: Alibaba Group is accelerating the rollout of its next-generation Zhenwu V900 accelerator by about six months as it expands a vertically integrated computing platform spanning processors, networking, storage and data centers.

items.title: DeepSeek bets on Huawei chips for model training as Nvidia's China sales slip
items.summary: DeepSeek CEO Liang Wenfeng said during a call with investors that he aims to rely on Huawei chips to train the startup's models in the future, and that a batch of training chips from Huawei are set to begin arriving at his company as early as the fourth quarter of 2026.

items.title: DEEPX targets smart glasses with low-power NPU, eyes 6G AI RAN
items.summary: South Korean AI semiconductor company DEEPX is reportedly conducting a proof of concept with a US smart glasses company to test whether its low-power neural processing unit (NPU) can balance power consumption, thermal performance, and AI computing capability.

items.title: Micron Taiwan union heads for strike vote as board, earnings calendar stall profit-sharing talks
items.summary: The labor dispute at Micron Taiwan continues to escalate after Micron and the Taiwan Taoyuan Union failed to reach agreement at a second mediation meeting on September 21, 2026. The union said the company has not presented a concrete profit-sharing plan and announced it will launch a strike vote under the Act for Settlement of Labor-Management Disputes, while Micron said it will keep talking and coordinating but must still go through board procedures.

items.title: Xiaomi open-sources MiMo-V2.6, publishes the bill for scaling reinforcement learning
items.summary: Chinese labs have spent the year arguing that reinforcement learning, not pre-training, holds the next gains. Xiaomi has now put a price on that argument. The company released and open-sourced its MiMo-V2.6 series on September 22, after livestreaming the reinforcement learning post-training run that produced it — publishing step counts, token consumption, and a running cost meter on a public page as the models trained.

items.title: Alibaba expands full-stack AI push as cloud data centers target 20 GW by 2032
items.summary: Alibaba Group Holding Ltd. doubled down on its full-stack AI strategy at the 2026 Apsara Conference, which opened on Sept. 22 at the Hangzhou International Expo Center. Alibaba Group chairman Joe Tsai made a rare appearance at the opening ceremony and said AI is moving from frontier exploration toward real-world deployment and large-scale applications.

items.title: BOE looks beyond displays with glass substrates for AI packaging
items.summary: Chinese display maker BOE Technology is expanding beyond its core panel business. Chairman Chen Yanshun said at the BOE Global Innovation Partner Conference 2026 on September 22 that the company's glass substrates are undergoing customer validation, marking a shift from technology development toward customer adoption.

items.title: Samsung weighs 4nm expansion as HBM4 demand strains capacity
items.summary: Samsung Electronics is considering expanding its 4nm foundry capacity as rising HBM4 base-die demand pushes existing capacity to full utilization, South Korea's Money Today reported on September 21. The company is also reviewing whether to build a new 2nm production line for base dies in future HBM5 products.

items.title: TSMC, ASE break ground on Taiwan's first advanced packaging cluster in Kaohsiung
items.summary: Rising demand for advanced packaging tied to AI and high-performance computing (HPC) is driving development at Baipu Industrial Park in Kaohsiung, where construction has formally begun on what is billed as Taiwan's first advanced packaging supply-chain cluster. Led by TSMC, the park's first phase has already been fully allocated, and a groundbreaking ceremony on September 21 drew more than 20 semiconductor companies, including TSMC, Foxconn, and ASE.

items.title: Escalating risks, evolving safeguards: a chronological look at OpenAI's safety strategy
items.summary: As artificial intelligence advances toward greater autonomy, balancing capabilities with safety has become a central challenge for industry leaders. Emerging model behaviors and high-profile security incidents have prompted a continuous evolution of safety initiatives, internal engineering adjustments, and proposed joint testing efforts between major AI developers.

items.title: India's fifth chip plant goes live, capping Suchi Semicon's three-year buildout
items.summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi virtually inaugurated commercial production at Suchi Semicon's outsourced semiconductor assembly and test (OSAT) plant in Palsana, Surat, on September 17, alongside CDIL Semiconductor's assembly, testing, marking, and packaging unit in Mohali, Punjab. The two facilities take the number of semiconductor projects in commercial production in India to five, according to The New Indian Express, joining Micron, Kaynes Semicon, and CG Semi at Sanand in Gujarat.

items.title: Exclusive: China SiC capacity tightens, spilling orders over to Taiwanese foundries
items.summary: China's silicon carbide (SiC) end-market demand is expanding rapidly, driven by high-voltage charging infrastructure and AI servers. The surge in orders has tightened SiC wafer capacity in China, and some offshore companies seeking foundry partners there have reportedly been turned away, pushing spillover business toward Taiwan, where Episil, HYS, and Diodes are among the names cited as potential beneficiaries.

items.title: Taiwan advances major science park expansion to support AI, semiconductor growth
items.summary: Demand from high-tech companies for new research and manufacturing sites remains strong, prompting Taiwan to advance plans to expand Longtan Science Park by 104 hectares as the government seeks to accommodate continued growth in AI and semiconductor industries.

items.title: Brussels will put a public efficiency grade on Europe's data centers before it decides what to require of them
items.summary: Europe intends to triple its data center capacity within five to seven years. On September 21, the European Commission set out how it plans to monitor that expansion: a common EU rating scheme that will attach a public electronic label, covering energy and water use, to every data center in the bloc with at least 500kW of installed IT power demand.
